trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: A homeless man claims he saw someone in a blind alley wearing a crab mask. The person appeared well-dressed, not like someone living on the streets. The animated expression on the mask could change, as though the shell itself were the person's real face.

You're just about to enjoy your Mont Blanc and a rich cup of coffee when the argument at the next table gets louder. They're bothering you, sure, but one person's view does strike you as the more reasonable one:
"Those who withdraw from society are running from their responsibilities."
"There is no evil, only good that society has yet to recognize."
"A lover is the part of yourself that got lost among humankind."
"One must realize they were whole from the very beginning."

branch.text: So what are we even chasing.

branch.text: So what are we even chasing.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Are you alright?
Her friend nods, catching her breath. But Adèle cannot help but notice how pale she is—far too pale—beneath the yellowy glow of the street lamps.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Good. I knew you were tougher than that.
Adèle exhales, leaning toward the window to see the shadows fade behind them into the night.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hah. Even with twice the legs, they still couldn't outrun us.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Er, Mr. Vincent, yes? We bumped into each other yesterday, remember?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I appreciate the help. You came just in time! But shouldn't you still be in a hospital bed?

items.speaker: Vincent
items.text: There is no "impossible" in French. I was back on my feet in no time!
The driver lets out two short, rough laughs and slams on the accelerator again.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Bravo, sir. Glad to see you're doing well.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle ...
Her friend pats Adèle's shoulder, but she doesn't notice.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Did you notice anyone waiting outside the café earlier, Vincent?

items.speaker: Vincent
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle, please. Something feels wrong.
Adèle squeezes her hand, leaning forward, closer to the driver's seat.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Those lipstick marks on your passenger window. Rude, wouldn't you say?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: People really need to learn where to put their lipstick these days, huh? Funny that you got the same message, in the same spot, with the same smudges!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But I wiped it off yesterday. And how did it get here? Where did you get this car?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Or is this even real? Am I in a dream?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You're speaking nonsense, Adèle. How could this not be real? Have you been sleeping alright?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Enough, Cici! You're just a part of this nightmare like everything else!
Célia's eyes go wide. She's looking weaker by the moment, like a candle burning out the last of its wick.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Ah.
The car isn't moving forward or backward now. It seems to simply hang suspended in darkness.
Her dragon climbs up the seatback and leaps onto Adèle's shoulder.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: By   fire,   what   is   false   is   purged.
Under the flame's glare, the beast's fangs rip through the man's human shell.
The beast that once was "Vincent" leaps out the window, his twisted form swallowed up by the abyssal night.
Adèle's stomach twists. In the dark, she imagines fur, fangs—something larger, hungrier—draining blood from a fallen body.
It had waited, starving, until now.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle? Adèle! Adèle!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You—
Before she can react, her dragon's tail coils around Célia's arm. The flame flares for a heartbeat—no longer.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You're really—
Célia seizes her hand.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Listen to me, Adèle! I remember now. I know the truth about the Beasts of Gévaudan—

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Manus Vindictae cracked open the Archive of Imagery! That's what's been causing all the disappearances and madness! They're trying to destroy Paris!

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Don't trust Roseau, and don't come looking for me! Take this.
Something cold drops into Adèle's palm.
She looks down, instantly recognizing the diamond now hanging from the necklace.
A brilliance like that could never be matched. It was a legend, one that should be far beyond her reach.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What? Is this the French Blue?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But surely this isn't the real thing.

Yet everything she knows about her ancestral trade screams at her. It's inarguable. This jewel is authentic. But it's too sudden. Who would ever believe a treasure like that could just fall into their hands?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Just take it! There's so much more I want to say, but just remember this: the Archive of Imagery must stay closed!
Célia forces Adèle's palm closed around it.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Destroy the stone.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: —From   darkness,   light.
The heavy darkness in her mind lifts. Adèle looks around, her temples throbbing.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ugh. Where am I?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Take a deep breath.

Soft couch, bright crystal lamp, gentle scent of incense, a diamond in her hand.
Everything exactly as it was before the cleansing ritual.
Even Beryl, sitting opposite, looks down at her from the very same pose she had been in before Adèle closed her eyes.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Was that ... Was I dreaming?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Not quite. You plunged into the depths of your mind and uncovered the shadow lurking within.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I saw them—the Beasts of Gévaudan at the Café de Flore.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, did we cast the beasts out of my mind, then?
She freezes.
The diamond in her hand. It had been a smoky quartz, but now ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn, this isn't the crystal I chose! This is the one Célia gave me in the dream.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The French Blue ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But how is this possible?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Am I still asleep? Is this part of the dream too?

She hears her own voice trembling.
Instinctively, she looks toward Beryl—the only one left who might be able to help her.
But a glimmer of genuine confusion passes over Beryl's face.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You must be confused. There was no other crystal.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: That gem was already in your hand when you came in.
